text_fidelity_a:
Seagate BlackArmor NAS 220 2-Bay 2TB (2 x 1 TB) Network Attached Storage ST320005LSA10G-RK I needed something bigger than my external hard drive to back up my files on my home computer which runs on Windows XP. I'm just about of space and all I want to do is to move stuff from my computer to the Black Armor NAS data server. Looks like it just ain't gonna happen.

After finally getting the program to install I get to where I'm ready to transfer data. Everything is correctly hooked up hardware speaking. After clicking on the "Black Armor Backup" icon on my desktop I get to this point:

It asks: "What would you like to do?" I click on "Backup".
It says: "Data to backup selection" I click on "My Computer"

I click on the teeny tiny box in upper left hand corner that says "Disk 1". It automatically checks NTFS and FAT32.
I click on "next".

It gives me 2 options: to "Create New Backup Archive" or "Add to Existing Backup Archive". It has automatically selected "Create New Backup Archive" which is what I want since this is the first time I'm backing up my computer.

In the "Backup Location Box" I see a few numbers and letters plus the "browse" box. The "next" button is greyed out so I have to do something here...hhmmmm...
So I click on "Browse" and Click on "Download on Seagate Black Armor NAS".
Then apparently I'm supposed to generate a name though it already has one in the box.
I click on "Generate a Name" and the name in the box changes by adding "\Download\My Backup.tib
I click "O.K."

Then: The file name, location or format"\\blah\Download \MyBackup.tib" is not valid.
Please type the file name or location in the correct format.
(I've gotten several different error messages at this point, but somehow it later lets me go the blue box.)

It goes to a small blue box asking user name and password.
I type in the username and password that the paper sheet in the box which came with the NAS told me to use.
And then I get an error message saying exactly the following:

"\\generated name| Download is not accessible. You might not have permission to use this network resource. Contact the administrator of this server to find out if you have access permissions.

Multiple connections to a server or shared resource by the same user, using more than one user name, are not allowed. Disconnect all previous connections to the server or shared resource and try again.

O.K."

So, I'm not anywhere near being a technical expert at this stuff. All I want to do is move some data from box A to box B so that Box A has a lot more room to work with. I've wasted a lot of time messing with this and nowhere in the PDF manual can I find the solution. I got this for free from Vine so it's going back in the box and in the closet. I'm reconnecting my other external hard drive which never gives me problems.

July 28th - I had to uninstall BlackArmor software. It made it very difficult to boot my computer. I got a fuzzy gray/blue screen with BLACKARMOR plastered all over it. My mouse would not work properly. I could only go up and down if I moved my mouse back and forth horizontally. This was just too unnerving.
text_fidelity_b: Seagate BlackArmor NAS 220 2-Bay 2TB (2 x 1 TB) Network Attached Storage ST320005LSA10G-RK

text_fidelity_a:
CPR V5000 Call Blocker for Landline Phones – Stop All Unwanted Calls at a Touch of a Button - Join Over 1 Million Satisfied Customers This is my second review, because I just had to buy a second unit, thanks to my honored telephone/wireless provider. Loved the first one I bought and considered it indispensable. Then Cox decided to change all its landline customers to VoIP. I asked the Cox tech to install it on the gigantic space-gobbling, dust-collecting modem he deposited on my desk, and he said Cox wouldn’t touch anything that wasn’t Cox equipment. Besides, said he, it wouldn’t work with the new equipment, anyway. (This assessment, it develops, was...uhm...in error).

Cox was offering NoMoRobo to its new VoIP customers, and having seen good reviews of that service, I figured it would substitute for the CPR Call Blocker. Because I expected I couldn't figure out how to attach CPR gadgetry to the accursed modem, I donated the now supposedly unusable device.

Mistake.

NoMoRobo turned out to be an endlessly annoying bust. To block a call from a phone number, NoMoRobo has to let the first jangle ring through. This is how it identifies fake phone numbers. Unlike the CPR 5000, it apparently has no preprogrammed numbers; thus every pest's nuisance call just comes right through. And unlike the CPR v5000, it seems unable to identify rogue VoIP/IP rogue diallers, leaving you vulnerable to an expensive scam.

I do technical editing for scientists and mathematicians whose first language is not English. This work requires sustained, close attention. It is not facilitated by constant interruptions. So NoMoRobo's first-ring technology was a deal-killer from the git-go.

Then we have the problem that you can’t signal NoMoRobo that a number is bad with a push of a button. You have to go online to their Website and fill out a freaking form! You have to retrieve the offending number from your phone’s memory, type it into the form, report the caller’s name, say what time the call occurred…all of which adds the insult of time suck to the injury of phone scamming. As hoop-jumps go, it’s brain-banging pointless: the robocallers simply generate new numbers, potentially dialing you from every telephone number in your exchange. Or, for that matter, in any exchange.

With the CPR Call Blocker, if you’re on a cordless extension, you simply press the “Talk” button and then press #2; if you’re at your desk where the device is sitting, you don’t even have to pick up. Just reach over and press that big red “BLOCK” button.

The highly satisfying big red BLOCK button….

Normally I get at least a dozen nuisance robocalls a day, starting at 8 a.m. (or earlier) and running through till 8 or 9 p.m. That's a bare minimum. Yesterday I attached the new CPR unit to the phone system, fairly early in the afternoon. This task, BTW, proved to be *vastly* easier than I imagined it would be. Once the device was online, NOT EVEN ONE MORE NUISANCE CALL got through! Feeling suspicious, I dialed the landline number from my cell phone: it rang right through. That suggests the thing blocked four to six robocalls. Right now it's about 10 the next morning, and so far just one call has managed to get past the CPR device.
text_fidelity_b: CPR V5000 Call Blocker for Landline Phones – Stop All Unwanted Calls at a Touch of a Button - Join Over 1 Million Satisfied Customers

text_fidelity_a:
Misfit Phase Hybrid Wearables Smartwatch - Rose Gold I've been wearing a smaller type fitness tracker for the past 6 months. Just started wearing this Misfit and there's a few things I don't like about it and many things I love about it.
I will start with all that I really enjoy about the Misfit. I like how easy it was to pair with my phone. Even though it sits higher than my other tracker, I like that it looks like an every day stylish watch and not like a fitness tracker. And it's very comfortable to wear. The buttons on the sides are more low keyed and not that obvious that it is a fitness tracker.
Love the sleep tracker of this smartwatch. My other tracker wasn't as good as tracking my sleep.
Step tracking is right on track with what I am walking. Very important to me.
I am still learning all the nice functions that come with this Misfit. So far I love the call notification and the alerts. Like that I can play and pause my music without taking my phone out of my pocket. I am still working on learning how to work my home smart devices using the Misfit but, I know in time, and with practice, I will figure it all out. It's not hard, I've just been really busy with working and haven't had the time with working with all the fun functions.
I also love that I don't have to take it off and protect it if I'm out hiking and get caught in a rain storm. I'm out almost every weekend walking in some nature trail or another. So I get caught in a few unexpected downpours while I'm out.
Now some of the more difficult "to do's" with the Misfit...
Setting the time isn't impossible, just need a lot of patience.
Using a magnifying glass, and good light, helped me get the misfit logo centered in that itty bitty hole at the 6 oclock mark. Whewww...
The watch doesn't have a backlight. So it's so hard to see the time in low light, impossible in the dark.
I wish it was thinner than it is. I'm not used to wearing a watch, or a fitness tracker, that is as thick as this one is.
I don't like the color of the watch band that came with the rose gold colored watch. All the other colored watches comes with a matching band. This watch comes with more silver colored band and silver buckle. Just doesn't look right. Might try to get that band replaced with something that looks better.
So far I am loving the Misfit. Love hearing that customer support is helpful in case I have a problem, like many has, with the crystal shattering.
text_fidelity_b: Misfit Phase Hybrid Wearables Smartwatch - Rose Gold

The manufacturer claims that it supports multiple devices at the same time, that it has a long range of 490 feet, that the battery charge lasts "all day," which most of us would interpret as 8-12 hours or more, and that it has a noise-cancelling microphone and enhanced speakers to create "crystal-clear calls" in noisy work environments.

I have tried to pair it to both my phone and TV transmitter at the same time, and the TV transmitter does pair if the phone is paired. The range isn't as far as advertised. The battery charge lasts about 4-6 hours. It has excellent sound quality for receiving calls and listening to TV, but persons on the other end of a phone call often complain that they have trouble hearing me, so the mic doesn't work very well. This headset is really uncomfortable to wear, making it difficult to use it more than an hour. Also, be aware that the rechargeable battery is not replaceable when it dies.

I actually have a headset with similar functions that cost me about 1/5th the price, so I'm not convinced this product is worth the extra money.

text_fidelity_a:
jumper EZbook 3 Pro Windows 10 Laptop 13.3" FHD Bezel-Less, Intel Slim Ultrabook Portable, 6GB RAM 64GB ROM, Metal Shell Lightweight Notebook Update: I do really like this computer. It has smoothly integrated into my home network and I now quickly go to it for quick and easy browsing and/or controlling stuff in my house (particularly if the main computer is in use by somebody else or for some reason tethered. The great thing is that with the full power of Windows and third party software, it can be whatever you need it to be. The one negative I've found, though, is that the delete key is under the backspace key where you expect backslash to be (which is in turn beside the right alt key). For this reason, I've accidentally went into sleep mode a few times, which is annoying. You can turn off the power key (while running) in windows, but the delete key still isn't where it is supposed to be.

Original review:

Surprise! I actually love this computer.

I mean, I am a bit of a power user, so I have a big gaming laptop and a couple of servers throughout my house, not to mention a few purpose-built niche laptops. So while I was a bit skeptical of this machine before it came since I saw the low price tag, I think it's awesome for the right purpose.

I mean, I totally get what "Chrome Books" are trying to do - be low price, low weight computers that run basically "from the cloud". But who really wants a computer running Android? I mean, there are phones for that. So running Windows 10 is a great idea. (Not that I love Windows 10, but if you install Windows Classic Shell and tweak, tweak, tweak away...turn off all permissions, get rid of all the stupid crap they're trying to sell you, use an offline account, then it is almost as good as Windows 7).

Anyway, you don't get a lot of fancy new stuff, but what you do get is important: 1080p screen, mini-HDMI out (odd choice, would have gone for micro or even full, but whatever), 2 USB 3.0 (No C), a micro-SD card reader, headphone jack, and a M.2 expansion port.

64GB of ROM is pretty small, but they installed so little bloatware (just one program to make the touchpad better - I uninstalled it because I didn't recognize it, am paranoid, and figure I can adjust it with whatever is built into Windows) that you have ~45GB free. Should be enough for stuff like MS office and other junk you may want. But you know what, I have a 36TB NAS, and Windows works flawlessly with it, so if I'm using this as a home machine, it's not a problem. I don't much care for public cloud, so if I want to take this on the road, I can always stream (usually still reach my NAS) or just throw in an SSD (by the way, it only takes the small form factor) or a giant micro-SD card (although admittedly either of these factors takes away the fact that this item is inexpensive to begin with.

6GB of RAM is sufficient for a computer that is not meant to be a workhorse.

It's really thin and light and with a real keyboard is just delightful as opposed to dealing with a tablet; a tablet always disappoints me when I'm trying to get something done quickly. It also boots up fast due to NAND memory. It doesn't even look cheap or anything. It actually looks pretty good.

It has a regular "wall wart" type AC adapter instead of the usual laptop power brick. I like this, but the cord is a little short (on the other hand, it is likely easily replaced with something in my electronics closet) The barrel adapter goes into the right side of the device (which is not abnormal, but less normal than the back or the other side in my experience) and the unfortunate part is that it will partially fit into the stereo mini-plug port for headphones on the same spot on the other side, which is likely to cause some confusion.

The only apparent downside is that the keyboard seems...like it vibrates slightly. Like it's not held in tight enough or something. I mean, it does have nice keys and overall I like it, but it just feels slightly weird, although still much better than a tablet roll-out keyboard.

I actually really like this little machine. Not for my main computer or my only computer, but definitely for easy browsing, or a multimedia machine for a teen, or a school computer, a travel computer, whatever. I'd use it for plenty of things, happily.

If you're cool with the memory - and living off a NAS, an SD card, or the cloud - and you're looking for something small and usable, definitely give this some consideration.
text_fidelity_b: jumper EZbook 3 Pro Windows 10 Laptop 13.3" FHD Bezel-Less, Intel Slim Ultrabook Portable, 6GB RAM 64GB ROM, Metal Shell Lightweight Notebook

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Paperwhite – (previous generation - 2018 release) Waterproof with more than 2x the Storage – Ad-Supported When I was searching for a new e-reader after my first generation Nook lost its life, I began comparing the new Kindles to the new Nooks and I ultimately chose to go the Kindle route for appearance alone. At first I was torn between the more expensive Oasis and this Paperwhite, and I was also confused as to why there are so many Paperwhite versions available. I figured I’d compare the newest of both to make my final decision and although the Oasis has some light features I like, I chose this Paperwhite because the side bar (where you hold it and flip pages?) on the Oasis is just ugly to me. I don’t like that it’s only on one side making the whole thing off center. I primarily wanted a Kindle so I could get off of my phone more often to just read and I also needed something that provided a more natural experience for my eyes. My favorite feature of the Kindle is that I can put it on dark mode with the black background and white text. I even keep my iPhone at the lowest light setting with dark mode too to spare my eyes the brightness 24/7.

This Kindle is exactly what I’ve been looking for. It’s lightweight, slim, very easy to hold, and turning pages is a breeze. No clicking buttons, just a tap on the screen. I paired it with the leather amazon case in plum to match and it’s perfect. Sleek and beautiful. The light options are perfect for day and night reading, I can even see it perfectly with zero eye strain in a pitch black room. The screen looks remarkably like a real print book and it’s just so simple to use. I was initially concerned about the ads being too intrusive, but it turns out that they’re only on the lock screen and they just advertise books to read. I don’t mind them at all. My Kindle is only a week old so I can’t speak to much else yet, but I’ve been using it daily all week and the battery is at 97% right now without any recharge so that gives me hope for it lasting going forward. I’m very happy with so far and have found that because it doesn’t do anything like a tablet or phone would do, I’m reading more without such distractions. Leaving my phone down more too. Love it.

text_fidelity_a: SamData 32GB USB Flash Drives 4 Pack 32GB Thumb Drives Memory Stick Jump Drive with LED Light for Storage and Backup (4 Colors: Black Blue Green Purple) This unit does work, but it is too slow for me to recommend it to others. When writing music onto it from my Windows computer, the write speed was slow enough to repeatedly drop the data transfer rate all the way to zero. Other manufacturers' flash drives do not do that; they keep on going. The read speed is slow enough that it causes my car's infotainment system (2019 model year) to sometimes hang up. Indeed, at one point, it caused my backup camera to go to all black for a minute or two. Note that some other reviewers are apparently unware of what flash memory is like. It has a limited number of times that it can be written (rewritten), and it will wear out if you try to use it as a substitute for a SSD. It also isn't going to be nearly as fast as a SSD. Flash memory is most appropriate for putting mp3 files into your car's infotainment system and other applications that are write only a few times but read many times.
text_fidelity_b: SamData 32GB USB Flash Drives 4 Pack 32GB Thumb Drives Memory Stick Jump Drive with LED Light for Storage and Backup (4 Colors: Black Blue Green Purple)

text_fidelity_a:
LotFancy Laptop Cooler Cooling Pad with 5 Quiet Fans for 12-17" Notebook, Dual USB Ports Disclaimer: I was sent this product to evaluate so that I could write an informed review.

Actually this is my second LotFancy cooling pad, and I took it because I do like their products. I haven't had any bad experiences with them except for breaking off one of the little plastic stops that keeps your laptop from sliding off the pad when the rear is elevated, but that was entirely my fault. I left the pad on the floor and someone stepped on it. Can't blame LotFancy for that.

The design of this pad is kind of interesting. It has two controls, one for the large center fan and the other for the four smaller side fans. This, plus the width of the pad itself, allows you to use various sizes of laptop efficiently. If you have a small one, you never need to turn on the side fans. If you have a 17" one, they're in position to help you cool it. I'm curious as to why the green light (signaling that the center fan is on) is set so much lower than the light for the side banks. A strange feature, though not something I have a problem with. It's just odd.

The pad is adjustable to seven different heights (including flat), so you've got a lot of positions to choose from. I write in a variety of places around the house, so this is one of my favorite things about the pad. It allows me to work without having to find all sorts of things to prop my laptop on. The locking mechanism is solid. Since it's USB-powered, there's an extra USB port at the back so that you don't lose that functionality. Most cooling pads have some way of doing this, so it's expected rather than special. It's quiet, but it's far from super silent.

It's a good pad. Yes, some of the construction seems a bit flimsy, but my other LotFancy pad has held together just fine and I see no reason to think this one won't.
text_fidelity_b: LotFancy Laptop Cooler Cooling Pad with 5 Quiet Fans for 12-17" Notebook, Dual USB Ports

text_fidelity_a:
Mini Projector, CiBest Native 1080P Projector Outdoor, 2023 Upgraded 9500L Full HD Portable Projector, Small Home Movie Projector 200" Supported, Compatible with PS4, PC via HDMI, VGA, AV, and USB The projector works well in small rooms and projects well onto an empty wall. We had to use a binder to prop it up so the video would be high enough to watch comfortably. IF you do use a binder or another angled surface, at least one of the edges will be blurry so you'll have to adjust the keystone. Without the adjustment, think that one haikyuu scene where it zooms in on Aone's forehead as he goes to block the spike. The overall quality of the picture is fine, but the pixels could be finer because they're still kinda big. Also, the colors are not as vibrant, but they are still pretty good quality. While watching, the audio comes through the projector. IF you do use the audio through the projector, it is crunchy. I am talking crunchier than a freshly opened bag of frito's lays in a dead silent movie theater during a dramatic death scene. I would definitely suggest using an external speaker or audio output unless the projector's crunchy audio appeals to you and your loved ones.

tl;dr
could have more pixels
could have better color
definitely look into an alternative audio source
works well in small rooms
doesn't have to be super dark for the screen to show up (pretty bright)
text_fidelity_b: Mini Projector, CiBest Native 1080P Projector Outdoor, 2023 Upgraded 9500L Full HD Portable Projector, Small Home Movie Projector 200" Supported, Compatible with PS4, PC via HDMI, VGA, AV, and USB

text_fidelity_a:
AKG (A Samsung Brand) N700NC M2 Over-Ear Foldable Wireless , Active Noise Cancelling Headphones - Black (US Version), 2.6, Model:GP-N700HAHCIWA Ok I can be a bit of a headphone snob, but at a near $300 price point I have some pretty high expectations. I ran them through my standard audio tests and these passed every one with flying colors. Bottomline, where most wireless sets fail is with bass, either its lacking or they overcompensate for it at the expense of everything else. (I'm talking to you SkullCandy). These however managed to be astounding on bass without it being overwhelming. Deep rich sounds, but mid and upper still came in crystal clear. It was impressive.

They also manage to have noise canceling without the annoying hiss present in the high end SkullCandy set I recently reviewed. The AKG's are superior and even performed better than my beloved, but admittedly old Sennheisers. How they would match up against a newer pair I can't say though, I will fangirl all day over a high end set of Senn's, but these AKGs give them some serious competition.

The ambient pass-through was a welcome addition, and these paired effortlessly via blue tooth. The ear cups were comfortable, although warm like every other pair of closed noise-canceling headsets I've tried. I will be honest I tend to prefer an open headset, but that is more preference than anything to do with this set. The ear cups were smaller than other pairs I've worn, I'm petite so that wasn't an issue but if you got yourself some good sized ears keep that in mind.

So if you have $300 burning a hole in your pocket and need some very well balanced wireless headphones, I highly recommend.
text_fidelity_b: AKG (A Samsung Brand) N700NC M2 Over-Ear Foldable Wireless , Active Noise Cancelling Headphones - Black (US Version), 2.6, Model:GP-N700HAHCIWA

text_fidelity_a:
TCL 32S3700 32-Inch 720p Roku Smart LED TV (2015 Model) UPDATE 2/10/16: It has been 44 days since I first contacted TCL about my defective TV. It has been 17 days since I was told a new TV would be sent to me and would arrive in 5-7 days. I have had numerous phone calls and emails on 12/28, 12/29, 1/21, 1/25, 1/27, 1/30, 2/4, 2/5, and 2/8. Each time TCL is unable to answer my questions (has new tv been shipped, what is tracking number) and each time I talk with someone I am repeatedly put on hold and then dismissed because they can't answer my questions and cant confirm what is going on. This has been extremely frustrating and the time period, lack of communication within the company, and conflicting instructions told to me by employees are all unacceptable. I loved the TV but it failed and trying to get resolution from this company has been a nightmare.

UPDATE 1/25/16 7PM: About an hour after updating my review I was contacted by TCL. After two phone conversations and several emails a replacement is being processed with no shipping costs at my expense. If this occurs in the timely fashion expected, I will update my review and ratings accordingly.

UPDATE 1/25/16: A week after I got the TV it started having display problems. The screen would come on so dark that only by looking at it at a certain angle could you tell that it was on. It required a jiggle/tap on the top for the image to flicker on all the way. I contacted amazon tech support. They had me try a power off/unplug. I expressed concern that it appeared to be something internal failing. They said the recorded my comments and were willing to offer a refund. I really wanted a replacement and not a refund so I said I'd see if it stopped acting up. It did not. It got progressively worse and now never turns on correctly and no longer results to tapping and jiggling the TV. On

12/28 I emailed TCLsocial regarding my problem as it was getting worse. On 12/29 they responded asking for a phone number so they could call me. I immediately responded with my phone number. I received no calls. I was then extremely busy workign 16-18hr days 7 days a week. The next chance I got, I emailed them again 1/21. They responded that they hadn't received my phone number. I sent it again. They said I would "get a call within the day". As of 1/25 no calls, no missed calls, no voicemails no emails. I'm fed up. All I wanted was for them to replace my manufacturing defective item with a new one. Its terrible how poor their response at getting this dealt with has been. At least I know Amazon will make the refund quick and easy. But I will most certainly not be using the money to get another TCL brand if this is how they treat their customers. Picture below is my screen on "on". If you squint you can see a faint outline of the netflix box to the right of the flash reflection. This is not a brightness or display setting issue.

ORIGINAL REVIEW: Excellent TV, very simple and fast set up. Beautiful picture and great sound. Love the smart tv features. I have never and likely will never have cable, this TV allows me to access my netflix and amazon as well as use chromecast to access my hbo go and youtube. I do not have a roku device or account but I love this TV's features. The remote is a nice small size and very simple and intuitive. I highly recommend this model and am very satisfied thus far. The stand/base is very solid and easy to put together. The remote came with new batteries. The customization and ease of use of this TV are wonderful. Price was great and shipping was fantastic.
text_fidelity_b: TCL 32S3700 32-Inch 720p Roku Smart LED TV (2015 Model)

text_fidelity_a:
[Upgraded Version] Anker USB 3.0 SuperSpeed 10-Port Hub Including a BC 1.2 Charging Port with 60W (12V / 5A) Power Adapter [VIA VL812-B2 Chipset and Updated Firmware 9081] AH231 After having to practically rip the box to get this thing open, I set it up with my computer. The plug into the transformer is a little tight and I'm not sure it is entirely in. Though it's not moving. The computer did not recognize it at first. I do have a Sabrent 7 port hub plugged in to another USB slot on my laptop, but that is mostly filled with devices that are required for license verification (ilok, etc...) and it will only really take a powered hard drive even though it is powered.

Back to the Anker. I plugged in 2 Seagate 2 TB drives and a WD 2 TB drive, all bus powered. Once the computer finally recognized the Anker (I had to take the USB out and plug it back in) All three drives were quickly recognized. However after about 10 minutes I got a message that the last USB device I plugged in wasn't working and then the drives reconnected, except the WD This is the same behavior I was getting with my Sabrent that caused me to look for another hub. I was able to reconnect the WD by unplugging it a replugging it in. It is getting to be a very frustrating thing trying to find a USB 3.0 hub that can handle multiple drives.

I am running Windows 8 on an HP laptop. I will try this for a bit. I hope it doesn't have to go back because I had to damage the packaging to open it.

Update 12/2/16 - I've had this for 2 years. for the last year it has been a pain to use. The plug that was difficult to plug in now won't stay in. It turns off if I slightly move it. I'm looking for another one. Most of the spots are taken up by USB licensers, so when it stops working, it crashes my programs. very frustrating.
Updated 1/6/15: After keeping this plugged in, it is now working okay. I am not sure that some of the problems are not caused by my HP shutting the USB ports down as a power saver. I transferred a number of files from the WD to the Seagate using the Anker with no issues. It was actually very quick. However, I only had the 2 drives attached. I'm not sure there is anything out there that is any better. This is my 4th USB 3.0 hub I've tried and none of them really work well. And it could be my computer. But the whole point of a powered hub is that the computer doesn't have to support it.

7/16/16 Update
Still using this, but the plug doesn't like to stay in. I have to be very careful not to knock it out. Otherwise, it is still working well.
text_fidelity_b: [Upgraded Version] Anker USB 3.0 SuperSpeed 10-Port Hub Including a BC 1.2 Charging Port with 60W (12V / 5A) Power Adapter [VIA VL812-B2 Chipset and Updated Firmware 9081] AH231

text_fidelity_a: Techko S184S Ultra Slim Door Guard Alarm I used these while my husband was training out of state for a length of time. Both of the ones I used worked great the first night, but one went off by itself the second evening. Luckily, it was early enough to where it was still light out, and I was standing in the next room facing that direction when it went off. Otherwise, it would have scared the %$%@ out of me, thinking someone was near the door or trying to break in. I could see there was no one there, nor had there been when it first went off. The evening was still, there was no wind nor vibration, so I don't know what made it go off.  It does make a loud alarm sound, and it doesn't stop until you turn it off, so I'll give it that! It may have just been a fluke, but I didn't feel comfortable using it again. If I would have been in bed or asleep and it went off, I would have totally freaked!  I would suggest going ahead and trying these, but don't rely on them being perfect and be prepared just in case they go off by themselves.  I went ahead and went with a security system company, just to put my mind at ease.  It you can't do that at this time, I would give these a try.

text_fidelity_a:
SiriusXM Onyx Plus Satellite Radio w/ Vehicle Kit, Enjoy SiriusXM Through your Existing Car Stereo for as Low as $5/month + $60 Service Card with Activation So let's start out with that it's a nice step up from your standard car radio. I like the overall design and you can save up to 20 channels and have 5 saved stations that you can tune into to transmit your signal, which I find nice for those areas when you start picking up other radio stations and there is bleed through. I didn't realize this at first, but the radio does have an internal transmitter, though I don't know if having it directly plugged into a transmitter will make any difference. So far mine has done nicely without the help of a third party transmitter. The little screen is nice too. It is not a touch screen, but you can see it well during the daytime and I find that for me the brightness at night is just right, not super blinding bright, but not so dim that you can't see it either. The radio also works similar to DVR and you can rewind to play a song again.

Set up is fairly easy and the instructions are easy to follow as well. I'd say it may take 30 minutes to an hour tops to set it up (that includes tucking away cords and positioning it where you want it) and activating it.

It does not come with a remote, but I think it would improve the experience of going through the channels, especially when driving, so you can still keep your eyes on the road and change the channel if you are wanting something different from your presets. Also, I believe you have to have a Sirius dock/boom box of sorts if you want to bring it inside and play music. You can transfer this radio between cars too, depending on your setup though, you may want to have a secondary dock and antenna set up in the second vehicle so its easier to transition and your not having to drag the dock and accessories around from car to car.

Something to take into consideration if you are thinking of getting this radio or other xm radios is that if you are not familiar with the subscription charges, is that you will have to pay the subscription fee, your state tax and a royalty fee and there is an activation fee. So outside of tax, I didn't realize there were other charges with the subscription fee. Personally I went with the 10.99 subscription and my fees were estimated to be 14.99 (this will probably vary from location to location), so not too much extra on regular fees after the activation fee. Just something to know so your not caught by surprise.

If its really cloudy or if you are under something like a metal awning/covering, the signal will go out.

I think the only thing that I don't like about the radio is the antenna. The reason I don't like the antenna is because the cord is too long for how I use it. I keep the antenna inside my car and the signal works fine, but the cord is ridiculously long. It could be upgraded to a motorcycle antenna, which is about 8 inches long, compared to X amount of feet. For others this won't be a problem, because you may need every bit of that extra cord, so it just depends on how you plan to set it up.

text_fidelity_a:
Microsoft Sculpt Ergonomic Wireless Desktop Keyboard and Mouse - Black. Wireless , Comfortable, Ergonomic Keyboard and Mouse Combo with Split Design and Palm Rest. I'm a huge fan of Microsoft keyboards. Never been much of a fan of their office productivity software, but when it comes to keyboards, Microsoft fits my needs to a T. I'm using the Microsoft Digital Media Pro keyboard which (I believe) was discontinued years ago. A shame, since it has so many useful features.

But out with the old and in with the new. I tried and did not care for the previous generation of ergonomic split keyboards from Microsoft. At first glance the Sculpt looked to be a better design. The divide between the two sets of keys did not appear to be as pronounced, and my hands seemed to fit the keyboard very well. Love the feel of the pad on the wrist rest area!

Installation was straightforward, although getting the items out of the box was a challenge. I was happy to see that the necessary batteries were included - nothing worse than having to go hunt for batteries before you can start to use a new device.

The keyboard feel strongly reminded me of a laptop. For some, that may be a good feature. For me it is not. The flat keys and shorter throw makes typing feel "unnatural." I know that sounds vague, but it's the best way I can describe it.

This odd feel translated itself into a much slower typing speed - cut my throughput by about half. Since I write reports for a living, that's a rather big issue.

I also could not come to grips with the function key placement, size and meager supply of ancillary keys. That's a feature I love with my current Media Pro keyboard in that I can map pretty much any of the ample number of multimedia keys to any function I choose, or even a URL. For example, to start SPSS, Excel and WP I press one key. Another single keypress also opens my browser and my Amazon cart URL (and yes, the lettering on that particular key is pretty much worn completely off from use).

Still, if I was forced to, I could live with the keyboard. I could not, under any circumstances, live with the mouse in this set. Feels poor, lacks refinement, and far less versatile than my Logitech M500. I tried my best to get used to the Sculpt mouse, but just grew to hate it the longer I used it.

Now, my opinions are certainly affected by my current choices in keyboards and mice since I've been using them for years and years. I've changed PCs at least three times, but have retained the same keyboard and mouse since they have worked so well. If you have less keyboard/mouse "muscle memory" perhaps the Sculpt will fit the bill. The build quality seems decent, and if they are as reliable as other Microsoft keyboards, it will continue to work for some time. But for me, I just can't move the approval meter past "meh" for the keyboard and "dud" for the mouse. Three stars.
text_fidelity_b: Microsoft Sculpt Ergonomic Wireless Desktop Keyboard and Mouse - Black. Wireless , Comfortable, Ergonomic Keyboard and Mouse Combo with Split Design and Palm Rest.

Logitech Harmony 700 Rechargeable Remote with Color Screen (Black) [Discontinued by Manufacturer] Solid remote with major flaws. Yes, the battery does last a long time...no issue there. But there is no battery life indicator on the screen and you don't get any warning when running low. So unless you plug it in regularly (which defeats the purpose of long battery life) you go from working perfectly to dead with no warning. While plugged in a battery graphic with a bolt tells you it's charging, but doesn't tell you the % charged or when it is done. When you unplug it the battery graphic doesn't go away, and it doesn't return to normal operation. You can push all the buttons you want, the battery graphic stays on the screen and it doesn't work. The only way to get it working is to take out the batteries and put them back in. And after you do that, you have to go through the tutorial before you can start using it again (thankfully, it does retain the device programming). What a hassle.

And when is Harmony going to get rid of the remote assistant? Like previous models, it constantly asks you if you want to hide the assistant, and it won't operate until you answer. Does the assistant even do anything the help button doesn't? If Harmony is so in love with this outdated 1990s feature, just put an assistant button on the remote and keep the damn thing hidden unless WE decide to turn it on. And the ability to skip the tutorial would be nice too. Nobody wants to be constantly answering to their remote.

Harmony is very good at making initial programming of the remote easy, but seem to give up on the interface after that. Once I'm done programming it, I don't want to mess with it any more, and I CERTAINLY don't want it to interrupt operation. Do what I ask you to do, otherwise sit there and look pretty.

Sony STR-DN1050 7.2 Channel Hi-Res 4K AV Receiver (Built-in Wi-fi & Bluetooth) Had a STR-DN1040, which we liked. Had no problem getting it up and running in our dedicated home theater. It worked well and sounded great. However, after 8 months the HDMI board went out (common problem we've learned). It was still under warranty, so we sent it off to Sony. Sony was not going to have the parts available for more than a month, so they offered us a brand new STR-DN1050. Sony customer service was excellent and it's hard to knock them when they offer a brand new amp that is the next newer model. We only received the new amp this week, but so far we love it. It was easy to set up and get running. I like the on screen setup display for the amp. It was very easy to navigate through. I know that several reviews I read complained about their being fewer HDMI inputs than the 1040. To us that did not matter as it is in a dedicated media room that only has a Blu-ray, DirecTV, and an iPhone connected to it. It sill has the front HDMI in the event we want to make an impromptu addition, as well more rear HDMI inputs available. I also read about folks complaining that the remote controls less functions. I am content with the new remote, as I didn't really control everything from the stock remote anyway. We really like that when we turn up the volume on the new remote, a volume control is displayed on the video screen. The 1040 did not do that and we missed it since our previous Onkyo did. There were also some concerns that the AMP was not truly 4K compatible. We use an Epson 8350 1080p projector (http://www.amazon.com/Epson-PowerLite-Home-Cinema-Projector/dp/B0044UHJWY/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1426790549&sr=8-1&keywords=Epson+8350), so not having full 4K compatibility is not a problem. To us the Blu-ray and DirecTV HD programs look awesome.

For a mid-range/price I would absolutely recommend this amp. Of course you can spend more, but why? Since the last amp went out after 8 mos, I am going to leave this review with 4 stars until we get some time under it's belt.

If you want to make your life and set up so much easier, also get the Deadbolt Banana Plugs, 12-pair, By Sewell Direct: http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B006U3O566/ref=oh_aui_detailpage_o00_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1
text_fidelity_b: Sony STR-DN1050 7.2 Channel Hi-Res 4K AV Receiver (Built-in Wi-fi & Bluetooth)

Amazon Basics Rolling Laptop Case, Black So I wanted to get some mileage on this bag before posting my review. I have had this bag now for almost 6 months and have used it regularly.
I like the overall design of the bag, it has held up nicely, wasn't super expensive and took the weight of a backpack off my back (so a plus for those of us who have back issues).

It has 3 zippered sections to put your things in. The first zippered section on the front has 2 pen pockets, 2 small pockets you can put pens or other things in, 4 business card pockets with a pocket the runs behind the business cards and 2 larger pockets that run horizontal behind all of that. (Ill include pictures to help show what I am saying)

The 2nd section has a laptop pouch. I measured my laptop and its length is 15 inches and is 10 inches wide/tall when in pouch, but it is a 17 inch screen (horizontal measurement of laptop for those who don't know). The pouch is has a little bit of padding on the front and back, so your laptop is safe there. The bottom seems okay as well and my computer has not suffered any damage, but for some who are more particular about their tech, you may want just a thin layer of foam or other cushioning (depending on the size of the laptop, you may can it in a sleeve into the pouch). There is also room to put some files or a binder in this section as well.

The last section is large enough to fit a 3 ring binder in, though you might fit a larger one if you don't have anything in the center section. The inside measurements are 13 inches tall from bottom to under the zipper and 15 inches wide from inside corner to inside corner. The dimensions listed in the product description say 17 (tall) x 14.5 (long) x 7.5 (wide)

Moving along to the wheels and handles. The wheels seem pretty sturdy so far and I have not had any trouble from them. They also are not swivel, so this may be a no go for someone looking for a bag with swivel wheels. The cloth handle is sturdy and nice to have when having to lift the bag out of your vehicle or going up stairs. The extended handle has a little loose feeling (and may feel cheap if you have owned a more expensive bag, but from my understanding of others reviews of more expensive bags, this seems to be a common complaint about the extend handles), but from my experience with it, it has served me well and has not given me any trouble. Also I am 5'5 and the handle is just right. My supervisor has the same bag and he is probably around 6'5 and the handle extends out far enough for him too.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics Rolling Laptop Case, Black

Yamaha Audio SR-C20A Compact Sound Bar with Built-in Subwoofer and Bluetooth This SR-C20A is an entry-level Yamaha soundbar made for the smaller room and bedroom. The attraction to this model was the 3rd speaker, a powered subwoofer.

Most compact soundbars create bass through passive radiators integral with the bar … i.e. 2 powered speakers separated in width by a baffled tube radiating through holes. So, there is no controllable bass other than passive baffle sound effects.

The SR-C20A has a controllable powered subwoofer and a dual baffle radiator combined to deliver controllable high, medium, and low tones. There are five modes: standard, stereo, game, movie, and a virtual surround mode. I just picked the one that sounds best. The virtual surround provides a sense of depth and separation to my hearing.

The SR-C20A soundbar replaced a no-name 2-speaker with baffles. The difference is sizable sound improvement.

Easy install, lots of input options.

Better sound than expected. Impressive sound. Sized for the smaller room LCD/OLEAD TV. Priced right.
text_fidelity_b: Yamaha Audio SR-C20A Compact Sound Bar with Built-in Subwoofer and Bluetooth

Actiontec 300 Mbps Wireless-N ADSL Modem Router (GT784WN) DO NOT BUY THIS PRODUCT. I am a Centurylink/Qwest customer of over 25 years. I have a old Actiontec Q1000 router/modem. My DSL Ethernet connection to my desk top has gone down for hours at a time lately. My wifi goes out 10-12 times daily as of late. Small one story house with only two old, non gamer people with latest model $800 smart phones. I read the online instructions and even watched Actiontec video for installing this product. I had a problem and called 1-888-436-0657 the tech support number listed in the Quick Start Guide. Actiontec's phone answering tree makes it very clear that they will not provide any tech support for products purchased from Amazon or any other "unauthorized dealers". I pressed 0 and they hung up on me three seperate times. The Amazon listing for this product made it very clear that it would work with Centturylink. It has a big check mark for Centurylink.

I have spent so many hours on the phone, through email and chat mode with Centurylink it is embarrassing. I offered to pay Centurylink to have a tech come to my home and install my new router/modem. Centurylink said their techs were not allowed to install router/modems but would check my outside wiring for free and my inside wiring for $85 minimun. Centurylink told me they would be happy to have a tech walk me through my hookup via telephone. After I finally was connected to a Centurylink tech and was verified they advised me they were not "allowed" to offer tech support to their customers on this product. They made it sound like it was a federal felony to offer tech support on this product.

Best Buy in New Mexico, and apparently all other retailers no longer carry any products compatible with Centurylink DSL because of their refusal to offer tech support. I heard that Amazon is having so many issues with router/modems that they are reluctant to take returns. I guess I will be taking the $67 loss. I should have rememberd my latin "caveat emptor".

So now I am going to angrily switch to the second most hated consumer corporation, Xfinity. Did you know that Xfinity is Comcast with a new name? Comcast's reputation is so trashed they decided if they adopted a new name they could fool a lot of consumers. As we all know, there is no real free market with open competition. In most markets you have DSL with the only telephone company available or cable with the only cable company in your neighborhood. A pig with lipstick is still, after all just a pig. I am advising myself and everyone else to do serious due diligence before purchasing any internet electronics from any vendors. Or you could just rent the overpriced and low quality products peddled by the ISPs.
text_fidelity_b: Actiontec 300 Mbps Wireless-N ADSL Modem Router (GT784WN)

text_fidelity_a:
Arlo - Wireless Home Security | Night vision, Indoor/Outdoor, HD Video, Wall Mount | Includes Cloud Storage & Required Base Station | 1-Camera System (VMS3130) Arlo is not perfect, but it is wicked close.

What's Great: You can put it anywhere within range of the link/router. The alerts are reliable, if a little slow on the uptake. The picture is good. Set up was simple and worked the first time. A reasonable amount of cloud storage is free, and it's easy to download whatever you want to save. The cameras are easy to move around to wherever you need them, and you don't have to set them up again.

What's Okay: A person who walks fast can get through a room almost faster than Arlo can start recording. Now, it's still much faster than an old Belkin Netcam HD, which sends pictures of where the motion WAS. Before the picture. And the D-Link 930L, which is a fine monitor cam, but has never been able to send a snap or a clip, no matter how many times it has been set up to do that. However, both of those cameras have audio and stream reasonably good images via their apps (the Belkin video resolution is way better than the Dlink). That makes them okay monitors next to smart security sensors - if the sensor alerts, you can look to see what tripped it and listen to see what's going on. Arlo will - most of the time - catch whatever set it off and let you know within seconds. And it's free, not an extra $$$ feature.

What Could Be Better: The link thing is enormous. It could be a little less expensive. And it would be WONDERFUL if it integrated with Z-Wave or Smart Things. The plan here is to station the Arlo cams near other devices that send push notifications - Nest Alarms, Smanos smart sensors, etc.

How It Compares: Beats the Canary I couldn't get to activate. Way better than the other netcams in the house. Love it. Just added another camera.
text_fidelity_b: Arlo - Wireless Home Security | Night vision, Indoor/Outdoor, HD Video, Wall Mount | Includes Cloud Storage & Required Base Station | 1-Camera System (VMS3130)

Google Pixel Slate 12.3-Inch 2 in 1 Tablet Intel Core i5, 8GB RAM, 128GB, Aspect Ratio 3:2 The Pixel Slate is Google's computer of the near future. It is great for some people right now, but not for everyone. Google has had their Android tablets and Chromebooks for many years now. The Pixel Slate combines those two concepts into an evolving platform. The hardware is really great right now with great fit-and-finish, a very sharp colorful screen, very responsive touch sensors, and great sound quality. Battery life is very good (over 10 hours per charge). The software is evolving quickly. Google has already released many updates the Chrome operating system and I expect this to continue.

The main problem with the software is that the Pixel Slate is running two types of apps: Chrome browser web-apps and Android apps. The user interfaces for these two are slightly different, which can lead to user confusion. There are also interoperability problems between the two, which also leads to user confusion. For example, Android apps can share files by just clicking on the share icon. Sharing a file from a web-app to an Android app requires downloading the app to the local file system, then opening the Android app and hunting through the file system to find and open the file. Hopefully one day some kind of automatic sharing mechanism will be implemented. Another confusion is that some web-apps and Android apps have the same name and functionality, but don't work the same. For example, Amazon Kindle has both a web-app and an Android app. If I download a book in the Kindle Android app, the Kindle web-app cannot find it, so I have to remember to use the Kindle Android app.

Who should buy a Pixel Slate? Google initially announced 4 versions of this product: one with a Celeron CPU, one with a Core m3 CPU, one with a Core i5 CPU, and one with a Core i7 CPU. I have the i5 version, which is plenty fast and responsive for anything I'm trying to do (I am not a gamer).

Apparently, the performance of the Celeron version was so bad that product has been cancelled. Prices now range from $800 to $1600, not including accessories like the keyboard or stylus. Even the $800 version is a lot of money, especially when you consider that a very good Chromebook can be had for much less money and that has a built-in keyboard. I have to imagine that the only people who should consider the Pixel Slate instead of a high-end Chromebook are people who will regularly need to use this device as a lightweight tablet. At just a pound or so, the Pixel Slate's tablet mode is much lighter weight and much less bulky than any Chromebook, even those flip-over style Chromebooks. If you can't imagine life without a physical keyboard, then get yourself a good Chromebook instead of the Pixel Slate.

The physical keyboard is not included with the Pixel Slate. Amazon sells a couple of different versions, but both have flaws, as well as very high prices. For now, I'm using a Belkin USB keyboard when I'm using the Pixel Slate at my desk. When I'm on the go, I use the tablet in touch screen mode without a physical keyboard. If a better physical keyboard comes along, I'll rethink this setup.
text_fidelity_b: Google Pixel Slate 12.3-Inch 2 in 1 Tablet Intel Core i5, 8GB RAM, 128GB, Aspect Ratio 3:2

PHILIPS Active Noise Cancelling Headphones Wireless Bluetooth H6506 Flat Folding Lightweight Over Ear Wireless Headphones w/Multipoint Bluetooth Connection 30h Playtime with Deep Bass for Home/Office They did a quality job on these. Luxury without excess. Packaging is acceptable. The case feels great, the zipper is awesome. The headphones fit in very easily, and there is a mesh pouch inside for accessories.

The headphones have a giant L and R printed on the interior foam, which is convenient to figure out which way to put them on, but isn't visible once they are. The buttons are easy to access, labeled, and simple enough to remember.

Bluetooth was easy to connect and had audio cues.

I'm usually not a fan of gesture controls, but they work really smoothly and intuitively here.

The product itself feels high quality, and they're very comfortable and secure. Noise cancellation is fine, and a nice addition, but I don't find it notable. What was more impressive to me was just how little I noticed the usual irritations of wearing headphones. They don't have a background noise at all, they don't feel like they're going to fall off if I bend over or make a sudden move, they don't press uncomfortably, and they don't make noise when I turn my head.

I've tried a few modern wireless noise cancelling headphones, and I'd say some of the others win in one feature or another, but these are an excellent complete package.
text_fidelity_b: PHILIPS Active Noise Cancelling Headphones Wireless Bluetooth H6506 Flat Folding Lightweight Over Ear Wireless Headphones w/Multipoint Bluetooth Connection 30h Playtime with Deep Bass for Home/Office

text_fidelity_a:
PANASONIC Wings Sport Headphones are Ultra-Light Wireless Bluetooth Sport Earbud 3D Flex Sport Clips with Microphone and Call/Volume Controller, IPX5 Rated Water-Resistant - RP-BTS35-K (Black) I received these earphones from Amazon Vine in early January, 2018. I liked the over-the-ears design. It makes the earphones far less likely to fall off when exercising. The sound quality is also excellent. I found its wireless bluetooth function quite handy for listening to music on my smartphone while walking, biking, lifting weights or doing calisthenics.

In short, as long as the battery could be charged, these sport earphones worked quite well. But suddenly, a few weeks ago, after only 7 months of use, the battery simply would no longer take a charge. The manual says that the battery should last through up to 300 charges, and there is absolutely no way that in only seven months I charged this device 300 times. It holds a charge well while the battery is working, much better than the other bluetooth earbuds that I have owned. So I could use it for up to five days without charging the battery. This means that, in seven months, I only charged the battery about 42-50 times, at most. This means the life of the battery was a mere 16% of what the manufacturer promised!

This is not a device in which the battery can be replaced. Therefore, once the battery dies, the earphones are worthless. Since the warranty is only for 90 days, there is no recourse with the manufacturer for replacing this device after that length of time.

The way that this product works is a good idea, but until the design includes the possibility of replacing the battery, the high price is simply not worth it. I will have to stick to cheap earbuds which are not such a hit to my pocketbook when their non-replaceable battery dies.

I rate this product as follows:

Sound quality 5 stars
Durability of battery: 1 star
Value for price: 1 star
Overall average: 2.3 stars
text_fidelity_b: PANASONIC Wings Sport Headphones are Ultra-Light Wireless Bluetooth Sport Earbud 3D Flex Sport Clips with Microphone and Call/Volume Controller, IPX5 Rated Water-Resistant - RP-BTS35-K (Black)

HAOHUNT Camcorder Digital Video Camera HD 1080P 30fps 3.0 INCH Touch Screen 24MP Camcorder with Microphone and Wide Angle Lens Vlogging Camera with Remote Control Infrared Night Vision Recorder This digital camcorder has features not found on many camcorders.
First the things I like about this Camcorder:
This camcorder records in high definition (1020 at 30 fps), and two low resolution (720P at both 30 and 60 fps) select-able from the screen.
There is a option for setting the camera up for motion control triggered recording.
The system has a IR based night vision system to record in total blackout conditions.
The remote can be used to control most modes of the camcorder and start/stop recording.
This system comes with a external mic to help in recording the audio component of your filming, you have the option to use this mic or not depending on your circumstances.
You can use the camcorder as a photo camera with resolutions ranging from 5mp to 24mp along with settings for white balance, color, and shutter speeds.
You can turn off the beep sound for camera functions, something you may use if recording wildlife.
This Camcorder comes with a wide view lens, great when recording in a shallow area such as a room to get everyone and everything into one shot.
Extra battery, handy for extended use or areas where you cannot recharge the camera.

Things I would like to see improved:
The zoom is digital only, not an optical zoom. This limits the camcorder to recording only items in a shallow depth, not great for outdoor use unless you are up close to your subject.

All in all, a decent camcorder for use where you are close (physically) to your subject, or as long as you understand its limitations.
text_fidelity_b: HAOHUNT Camcorder Digital Video Camera HD 1080P 30fps 3.0 INCH Touch Screen 24MP Camcorder with Microphone and Wide Angle Lens Vlogging Camera with Remote Control Infrared Night Vision Recorder

Speed wise any SSD is good. I also own a Crucial M500 that I installed in my Linux laptop with SATA I, which is reported to be much slower but in practice proved to be x10 faster than the original laptop hard drive. For all of my other computers what makes the Samsung nice is the software. With Samsung Magician Software I can adjust over provisioning and see if any updates are needed. It also gives you a lists (profiles) of some items that you might need to adjust in your OS to make the SSD run optimally. It will also show you the health status, how many writes have been made and it can do a speed benchmark (though this can be done by other free software too). Samsung also provides migration software, but I never used that since I prefer to install from scratch.

Of course the brand reliability is probably the most important. I wouldn't touch OCZ drives for example, even if they were free.

text_fidelity_a:
Panasonic DMP-BD87 Ultra-Fast Booting Blu-ray Disc Player When we first tried it, the streaming was awful. It couldn't hold a connection to Vudu, to Hulu, or to Netflix.

We ran an update--tricky because it didn't readily hold a solid network connection--and things improved considerably. I can stream Hulu with minor hiccups, Netflix without issues, and Vudu except at 1080p. For the record, I can stream Vudu at 1080p on the TV that the player is connected to. It still supports only a small subset of services, though Hulu has been added. As a streaming media player, it doesn't meet expectations. As a simple blu-ray player, it is quite excellent for the price. It was able to play a few old, slightly scratched DVDs that other players were having trouble loading.

On the signature features, I could find no appreciable difference in boot up or launch time between this and my Sony, or between this with fast boot turned on and this with fast boot turned off. Blu-ray players tend to boot pretty fast in any case. This one allows up to four users to have customized interfaces, but it only affects the background image and color scheme of the interface screen. It does not allow four users to each maintain their own login to Netflix or Hulu, which would be useful if Netflix ever allowed multiple users of an account to maintain their own Watch Instantly queue the way they do with DVD queues.
text_fidelity_b: Panasonic DMP-BD87 Ultra-Fast Booting Blu-ray Disc Player

Bloody M90 TWS Active Noise Cancelling Bluetooth Gaming Earbuds, Hybrid Carbon Diaphragm, Bass Music & Low Latency Gaming Mode, Dual ENC Microphone, IPX4 Rate, with Wireless Charging Case I’ve been using the Bloody M90 Earbuds for about a month, and I’m quite impressed with them! I usually prefer over-ear headphones because they are more comfortable for me -- I have quite a few inner ear piercings -- but I’ve barely used any other set of headphones for the past month.

Once you find the right size, these buds are comfortable and stay in your ears. The box includes three sizes of ear tips: small, medium, and large. I did have a short adjustment period, the noise cancelling made me nauseated. This is not a fault of the earbuds, it’s something that can happen, and within a week, I was able to wear the earbuds for hours at a time.

I use the earbuds to listen to music and stream shows. I’m not an audiophile, but I think the sound quality is pretty good. Music sounds clear and punchy, no tin can or thin bass here. The noise cancelling is not as robust as a pair of over-ear headphones, but it dampens enough of the background noise in my home that I can clearly hear what I have playing.

The main advantage of these earbuds is they don’t give me a headache like over-ear ones do after a few hours. There’s no headband sitting on top of my head, or squeezy tight ear cups. As I mentioned, I have a few inner ear piercings (tragus, rook, daith) and I’m still able to wear the earbuds comfortably. They stay in while I walk around the house.

I can use one earbud or both, and they have tap controls. They connect easily, all it takes is opening the case and they’re connected to my computer.

The case is pretty swanky, matte black with a thin strip of metallic red. The case has 4 small LEDs on the front to show battery and charging status, the lights go on when opening the case or when it’s charging. The case works with wireless charging or via USB-C, a short cable is included.

The instructions are easy to understand. The Quick Start guide was all I needed to get up and running.

Still, I have a skin on the keyboard as protection against any liquid OR dust OR hair getting into my keyboard that I have been using since 2008 when it was new.

My replacement (Allinside) is now in place and I can once again see the keys.
The skin fits the keys such that it does NOT have to wrap around the edges of the keyboard.

UPDATE (7/14/2018): After one year I have to replace this keyboard skin because it is wearing out in several places, mainly the left side command key where there is a ¼ inch slit. When I have to type a long document / letter, I remove the skin so I can type faster on the aluminum keyboard because the keys require only a light touch. I have not switched to a BT keyboard because this one is so good, and the fact that it is wired is not a problem with a little tape to keep the cable out of the way when I slide the keyboard shelf in and out. The skin I received is transparent with nothing printed on any of the keys.

For those who have the wired Apple aluminum extended keyboard (with keypad), this product fits correctly to protect the keyboard from dust and spills. It is in use on my Mac Pro (early 2008). The description says for iMac, but it fits any of these keyboards of this style, not just the iMac keyboard.

It arrives folded, but that does not matter if it comes from a seller in the US who delivers it in a timely manner.

The keyboard cover does make it necessary to slow down the typing speed. That's not a real problem unless one is a touch typist or writer who spends a lot of time on the keyboard.
text_fidelity_b: ProElife Ultra Thin Silicone Full Size Keyboard Cover Skin for 2017 2018 Apple iMac Magic Keyboard with Numeric Keypad MQ052LL/A A1843 US Layout (Item Folded in Packaging) (Ombre Blue)

text_fidelity_a: Beyution V4.1 Bluetooth Headphones Wireless Foldable Hi-fi Stereo Headphone for Smart Phones & Tablets - Black I purchased and received these Beyution V4.1 Bluetooth Wireless Foldable Hi-fi Stereo Headphones - Black for $20.99, delivered free with my Prime membership.  This bluetooth receiver, in ear buds or headphones is the best I own or have purchased.  I use them mostly for watching TV, silently in my home living room, early and late.  The are kind of tight fitting on my ears, , but do have soft ear pads.  Each side adjusts an extra inch of fit size and this is adequate for my big round head.  I would recommend them to be folded when they are at their smallest size, as it is kinda flimsy when full opened up.  The controls are on the bottom of the left side; power on/phone button, aux input jack, charge micro usb port, and forward/back/play/pause slide button.  I like them and feel the price with delivery is a pretty good deal.  They sound pretty good when you are listening to Bluetooth, a signal that is not too good for audio fidelity quality, so don't expect plug in quality as a bluetooth receiver.  This headphone can be plugged in and used as a regular cabled set of headphones also.  The bluetooth has the best range of any bluetooth receiver I own.  To hear what they really can sound like, plug them in to the jack and listen to a CD or another high fidelity source, besides MP3, Bluetooth or "Radio" satellite, all sources which are notorious for poor fidelity,  as these are not great HiFi sound signals.  Sound has gone way down hill with these formats for electronics for the masses.  I don't listen to Bluetooth much or these other low fidelity formats with the music I like and if I did, I would prefer to use these headphones, rather than ear buds of similar price.  Of course, much more expensive products can be purchased, but I won't, as I have in the past and they are not worth the investment of my money.

text_fidelity_a:
KINESIS Freestyle2 USB Keyboard for Mac (9" Standard Separation), Black Overall this keyboard is great. The keys feel nice and they're quiet but not too quiet or soft or squishy. Enjoy typing on this keyboard, pushing the keys seems to take minimal effort and overall it's great.

The best part about the keyboard is that it separates and having the ability to give it a little separation is great. I miss it when I don't have it and it helps avoid torquing the wrists when you are typing. I also love the feel of the keys.

Now before my minor complaints understand two things: (1) I really like this keyboard and despite what I would consider minor defects, I would definitely buy another one. (2) please excuse the fact that I like my keyboards to be consistent and while Apple may not make the *best* keyboards I do use a laptop and I am used to their keyboard layout and feel.

The biggest thing that annoyed me when I purchased this keyboard was the positioning of the ⌘ (command) key. It seems to be shifted over a bit from what I'm used to. Normally I would hit ⌘ with my thumb but it's a little touch to do that on this one given the position of it. It's just something I'm having to get used to.

One minor downside to the keyboard is that the function key doesn't work the same way as the default apple keyboard, rather, the `fn` key is a toggle. I prefer for fn to work as a modifier because that is what I am used to on my laptop keyboard.

Another minor problem is the styling on the caps lock key. Like many people, I remap my caps lock to ctrl and and thus want caps lock to be a normal button. However, on this keyboard the caps lock key is missing the right part of the key so that you don't accidentally hit it when typing the `a` key.

Finally, the escape key and '`' (back tick) keys are in weird positions. The escape key is not as bad as the backtick. There is just something about the distance that I must go that is different from what I'm used to and I have been consistently hitting the `1` key instead. Life goes on.
text_fidelity_b: KINESIS Freestyle2 USB Keyboard for Mac (9" Standard Separation), Black

text_fidelity_a:
CozyPhones Sleep Headphones - Over Ear Headphones from Ultra Thin Cool Mesh Wired for Side Sleepers, Meditation, Running, Laptop, and Phone - Pink Lycra This sleep headphone band fits quite comfortably. Before I bought this I was introduced to the product at my mom's house and I wear a considerably bigger hat size than her, but the stretchy band fit both of us perfectly. Despite my big bobblehead of a noggin, I don't find this too tight even when worn for hours, and yet it hasn't become stretched out either. A smaller headed person could still wear mine. Also in regard to fit, the light weight, low profile speakers can easily be moved inside the headband to exactly where they are most comfortable and best heard for each wearer (I did have to move the speakers back when I tried my mom's). Once in place the speakers stay put really well simply due to the friction between the textures of the fuzzy fabric pad over each speaker and the headband's fabric. I occasionally have to tweak where a speaker is sitting as I put them on, but once in place the speaker has never needed to be repositioned during wear. I also love that the speakers can be slipped out through the back so the headband can be laundered.

I would say that the sound quality is that of average headphones. I don't notice a discernable difference between these and any other headphones I own, but I may not have as attuned an ear as some people seem to have, so my feelings won't be hurt if you get a second opinion on this part.

I don't really have any cons to mention for these, but wait, I almost forgot to mention that when buying these I saw multiple other reviewers warn that the dye bled from the colored edge of their headbands. I should say that I specifically bought the one with the white edge to avoid that happening. I've had no dye transfer at all from mine, so I can suggest getting the white edged band if that's a concern.

Hope this helps.
text_fidelity_b: CozyPhones Sleep Headphones - Over Ear Headphones from Ultra Thin Cool Mesh Wired for Side Sleepers, Meditation, Running, Laptop, and Phone - Pink Lycra

text_fidelity_a:
woednx Smart Watch,1.4''Full Touch Fitness Tracker with Heart Rate,Blood Pressure and Sleep Monitor,Message Notification,Smartwatch for Men WomenIP68 Waterproof Smartwatch Sports for iOS Android-Blue PROS

1. The silicone band is very comfortable. Apparently if it breaks, it can be replaced, though I’m not sure where or how you would buy a new band.

2. The appearance is sleek and modern, and the size of the watch face makes the digital numbers easy to read.

3. It has a rechargeable battery, which may have a longer life than the non-rechargeable batteries of most sports watches.

4. If you want a smart watch that is far cheaper than most brands, this might work for you.

CONS

1. There are three primary functions that I use a sports watch for: to instantly check the time, a stopwatch, and a timer. It irritated me no end with this watch that, after only a few seconds of being lit up, its face goes dark. While this might save the charge on the rechargeable battery, there are plenty of times when my right hand it not free to punch the button on this watch to light up its face, and I can’t quickly and conveniently check the time! It is also a hassle trying to use the stopwatch and timer functions.

2. I absolutely loathe the way this watch’s battery is recharged. Instead of using a standard C cable, the charging cable attaches magnetically, and it becomes detached far too easily. There is also no warning when the battery of this watch is about to go dead.

3. I don’t like the software this phone uses. It is a major hassle to learn for what I personally consider very little useful return. Why? Because most of the functions offered by this watch that are of any interest to me I can get through my smartphone. I use my phone and a Bluetooth for phone calls, texting, music, and hearing alarms. I check the weather by looking around me when outside or looking at weather apps on my phone. I use my phone for photography.
The rest of the functions this watch offers I personally find to be useless. I do not need a watch to tell me how to do a deep breathing exercises. As a healthy individual with no heart issues, I do not need to monitor my heart rate 24/7. (And if I did, I would use medical equipment that is far more reliable than this cheap watch.) I don’t need to obsessively monitor my sleep. (And, again, if I did, I wouldn’t trust this cheap watch to do an accurate job of it.)

4. Its pedometer function might have been of use to me, but unfortunately, it is inaccurate.

CONCLUSION

I dumped this watch and went back to a regular, inexpensive sports watch.
text_fidelity_b: woednx Smart Watch,1.4''Full Touch Fitness Tracker with Heart Rate,Blood Pressure and Sleep Monitor,Message Notification,Smartwatch for Men WomenIP68 Waterproof Smartwatch Sports for iOS Android-Blue

Amcrest 720P Wireless IP Camera WiFi Security Surveillance Camera System, HDSeries Indoor Camera for Baby Pet Nanny Monitor, Plug/Play, Pan/Tilt, Two-Way Audio & Night Vision IPM-721S (Silver) This item is a good choice IF you only want to install ONE SINGLE CAMERA. Multiple cameras drops you through a black hole into an alternate universe where nothing works or configures. I tried to install two of these over a period of four days and each time, some different and annoying glitch came up to prevent the things working as a system.

When installing two or more cameras and using WiFi as the way they're connected, each camera has to be located where the WiFi signal is strong or it will either not work or will respond slowly. This slow response is accompanied by ragged video images. Even installing a WiFi extender does not help, as the extender looks, and actually is, a different WiFi connection. To function together, and be viewed in side-by-side windows of the Amcrest View software, cameras MUST BE ON THE SAME CONNECTION.

In order to install the cameras, you need to download Amcrest View from the App Store (iPhones and iPads) or from Google Play (Android devices). The Lite version is free and wouldn't configure my cameras, nor did it provide the level of camera control I needed. I ended up purchasing the Amcrest View Pro app for $0.99 and even this did not allow me to successfully setup a dual camera system.

One of the cameras needed to be in a spot where WiFi was weak so I decided to link it up hardwired to the network. That requires using a tool from Amcrest called IP Config. I tried to install the IP Config software (supposedly on the CD that comes with the camera) and Windows promptly told me the folder was empty. I downloaded the install from the Amcrest website and the app ran but DID NOT install the IP config software on the computer. And, yes, I tried multiple times.

Several calls to tech support resulted in no useful resolution. Each tech told me something different. One, even wanted me to download and install a third-party app so he could take control of my PC. As he seemed to know very little about his subject matter and computing, I declined. The TECH SUPPORT IS AWFUL. After waiting in a long queue, I spoke to reps NOT IN THIS COUNTRY, who really did not understand my questions--a language issue--so they were of little use and just people in some other country doing a job that should be being done by someone living in, and contributing to the economy, of the United States.

I finally gave up on these cameras and sent them back. I will not ever purchase an Amcrest product of any sort again.
