text_fidelity_a:
WD My Net AC1300 HD Dual Band Router Wireless AC WiFi Router Accelerate HD UPDATE: Since the review below this paragraph, I have put this up without a backup, and it's been a fire and forget mission. No problems with wireless network service. My "OK" review still stands, but I'm still optimistic some firmware upgrades or a big "that's it!" on my end could get everything working better or even flawlessly.

I have an extensive wired gigabit network in my home, so it has not been my top priority to replace my antiquated wireless B/G router (although I do use it much for casual surfing, mind you). Because I've been very busy when at home lately and in no mood to deal with nuisance computer/network issues, I put this new router in parallel with the old so that if issues came up, I wouldn't have to deal with them immediately. After about three weeks, albeit with only casual and sporadic "trying to make it work right", it's still not ready to run solo, obviously reason enough to just rate average.

This is unfortunate because it has a lot of cool touted features. The funny thing is when I was first setting it up I was thinking how they really have it idiot-proofed - even the WAN port is color coded to the included network cable (they don't even call it a WAN port, BTW).

But as is so often the case, by trying to make something useable to the masses, it actually becomes more difficult for advanced users to do simple tasks: I sort of want some Network Attached Storage (NAS), but have been too cheap/lazy/power misery to want to bother dealing with it, so I thought it would be great to try this router with its USB ports - ideally, I was going to put some hard drives in my gun safe, which is beside my telecom closet, and attach them to the router via USB, and have them both set to turn off when not in use. But it's just not working. I could go into a rant here about how Windows tries to set up a GUI so that people ignorant to computers can access their media when I all I really want to do is access the root of the drives and then do what I want without interference, but I'll save you my usual rant because I don't want you to misinterpret that it is indeed the router's fault that it rarely recognizes my attached devices (although interaction with various versions of Windows is the fault of both companies). The fact is, from the router's access page, you can see that my drives are often not recognized at all, or the router still thinks I have something attached that I've detached a while back (and sometimes even after a reboot). Clearly, I'm not about to put these drives down in a safe on another floor; it's easier just to deal with them locally. I was unable to EVER access these from a tablet or a phone; I wasn't about to waste that much time when I couldn't even rely on it to work with decent Windows machines.

The gigabit Ethernet ports are a great feature, and the wireless portion works better, but there have been a few times where I've checked my machines and they've reverted back to my legacy network, meaning that the new router obviously went down, if only for a short time. Thus, I'm not ready to put this machine up solo and deal with any headaches that I may have to incur.

With some cool features like QoS (Quality of Service) and port forwarding, etc., it sounds like it could be a great router. I can't begin to test these well when I'm still frustrated with making it look like a real seamless network. These are probably things that can and will be fixed with firmware updates, but they should have had this ironed out before release. If I hear of a good update, I'll give it another go if I'm still interested and will let you know how it works out.
text_fidelity_b: WD My Net AC1300 HD Dual Band Router Wireless AC WiFi Router Accelerate HD

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech G240 Cloth Gaming Mouse Pad for Low-DPI Gaming I'm not a gamer. I wanted to try this mouse pad out for graphics (photo editing, vector graphics, and so forth). I'm not a big fan of pen-type tablet input devices. I've always preferred working with a mouse. (To me, the only real down side to using a mouse instead of a tablet input is loss of pressure sensitivity, but there are plenty of workarounds.)

This pad works great. An optical/laser mouse reads it very well, with the slightest movements picked up. The bottom of the pad is grippy enough for the pad to stay put, and the surface, while satin-like, still has enough resistance to provide a lot of fine control.

It's also larger than I expected. It's 11 inches by 13.5 inches. And it is quite flexible and rolls up easily for storage or transport.

Here are some tips for getting precise mouse control:

First of all understand that a low-DPI setting means your pointer doesn't move far when you move the mouse. This enables gamers to aim and target precisely in-game. It also enables artists to precisely move the pointers when working on graphics. How far your cursor/pointer moves is entirely up to you and can be adjusted in your control panel for pointer settings (or, depending on the game, possibly can be adjusted in your game settings).

In that control panel, uncheck "enhance pointer precision." This will turn off pointer acceleration, which can adversely affect control. If the software (or game) you're using overrides this (rare in graphics software, but more common in games), you may have to employ a fix. Just do a search for "Windows 7/8 mouse fix" and you'll find plenty of information on how to do this.

Anyway, it's a great pad for precision cursor control with a mouse, whether for gaming or graphics.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech G240 Cloth Gaming Mouse Pad for Low-DPI Gaming

This is a 5-star lens but there is a slight issue I have with the autofocus and that being it is too fast. In the video attached to this review you may be able to see what I am saying. When recording video the lens refocuses very often if shot on autofocus. This is neither a good thing of a bad thing because it can be easily fixed shooting on manual focus, you just need to know that.

If you're wanting to shoot sports, shows, events, or anything requiring distance (about 50 yards max) then this is the lens to have. Yes it might be expensive but it is a great investment.
text_fidelity_b: Canon EF 70-200mm f/2.8L IS II USM Telephoto Zoom Lens for Canon SLR Cameras

TP-Link AC1900 Smart WiFi Router (Archer A8) -High Speed MU-MIMO Wireless Router, Dual Band Router for Wireless Internet, Gigabit, Supports Guest WiFi I wrote this review with a heavy dose of input from my husband, who is a retired IT professional.

We had a problem with the router supplied by our internet provider. It was causing all the devices on the network to lose their connection multiple times per day. The provider sent us a new router, but it was a "black box" device that did not allow for configuration by the user or even the provider's tech support personnel. So we decided to buy our own router. After quite a bit of research, we picked this one.

PROS

-Good speed at 600Mbps for the 2.4GHz band and 1300Mbps for the 5GHz band.
-It is configurable by the user. I can sign on to the admin page via my browser and change settings. The setting we most wanted to change was the default DHCP server lease time setting. For a home network such as ours that always has the same devices using it, there is no need to have short (i.e., hours long) DHCP lease time setting. The constant renewing of the lease can cause connection issues for the devices. At least, that has been our experience.
-The device seems very stable. Since swapping it in for the internet provider's router, we have had no dropping connections whatsoever. We are quite pleased with this router.
-2 year warranty.

CONS

-The maximum DHCP lease time setting was only a couple of days, unlike a previous router I had, which allowed you to go up to 30. But this is not really a big disadvantage. I have not noticed a problem with it.
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link AC1900 Smart WiFi Router (Archer A8) -High Speed MU-MIMO Wireless Router, Dual Band Router for Wireless Internet, Gigabit, Supports Guest WiFi

Fire Kids Edition Tablet, 7" Display, 8 GB, Blue Kid-Proof Case (Previous Generation - 5th) Very disappointed in Amazon. They ALMOST Got it right. Returned this one quickly.

Let me be clear I am an Amazon Fangirl. I have consistently tried their new things, I have subscribed to prime for years, I love amazon. I love their kindles. So I don't often speak ill of my precious amazon.

I wanted to upgrade my son's kindle ( First gen Fire HD7 ) it's charging port is a bit wobbly and damaged, we've used it for many years and it's got a little wear. That said, it works BETTER Than the current kindle fire. The only problem is you can't play all the same games that I can play on my other kindle and you can't on the new one either. It wants the "NEW HD" ( or my HDX) to play certain games.

Where to begin....first of all the new OS Sucks. It just does. so bad. I'm not even going to rant on that because it's user preference but I found the old OS to be more user friendly and responsive. I have an HDX and it's by far the top notch of them all. I hope I don't have to "upgrade" to this OS.

Storage & Offline use:
You only have 8gb of storage, which wouldn't be an issue thanks to the upgradable microsd slot.. ( GOOD CALL AMAZON) ..EXCEPT They crippled the functionality. For example, I go to the grocery store or road tip with my kid and I let him watch or play on his kindle without being on wifi, you can't do that anymore. Your kids can NOT Watch movies that are downloaded to the microsd card when you are offline. You can't. Not allowed. You can't operate much of anything in the kids profile if you are not connected to wifi. Having 128bg SD card is USELESS for your kids when offline.
I've bought loads of disney movies and the digital copies are all on Amazon for the very reason that they were great to download to our other kindles and watch when we were in the car, plane, or costco.

It won't even let you START The kids freetime profile if you are offline. This severely cripples the device for no good reason. Games and movies which are downloaded to the device or the SD card should work offline in most cases. I've done it on my HDX and my first gen hd. Works just fine in freetime on older devices. No reason for this. And before someone tells me that's what you expect when you stream...I'm not talking about streaming or using netflix, I'm talking about content downloaded to the device. Irrationally Amazon decided that if you are not online, you can go kick rocks.
If you are in an ADULT Profile, I think you can, although I did not try to be fair, because I bought the KIDS Edition for a reason, for my kid to use it.I have my own kindle. No sense in having this for kids if you can't use it when you're out and about. Everyone knows that the screen is the ultimate "quiet time" reward in our parent tool-kit. If you say it's not you're either a liar or an over taxed helicopter parent with way too much techno anxiety. Joking...sorry not sorry.

Kindle FreeTime "unlimited"....
I use the freetime for my son ALL THE TIME. It's amazing, it limits him to what *I* want him to play and watch. I can set a timer for weekends/weekdays that go off at bedtime so that he can "read", watch a show, or play for a short time as a reward before bed. The freetime is
the number one reason I have not gone with an iPad or other device. I can't give my kid any other device with the same level of comfort and control of his screen time and content. I HIGHLY recommend kindles to all my parent friends for this exact reason. It's WELL Worth it. However...it's NOT worth it to use "Unlimited" on this new device. The new kindle sucks for freetime ( See above reason on offline freetime) Mainly tho...it's TERRIBLE for the parent if you've mistakenly turned ON Kindle unlimited. ( If you have an older child, say 9yrs+ this can be mitigated with a nice sit down convo) I'll explain...

Why Freetime Unlimited SUCKS:
I'm speaking of the paid Unlimited service here, the main feature of freetime is still great, with some exceptions ( above) on the new device.

Every single app they touch it will download. If they are curious, and want to see what the game is they instinctively click the app, completely unaware that they have 8gb of space on their tablet and actually it's more like 4gb after the OS. This makes it run Slooooooow and crash. Crash a lot. Crash within the first 60 minutes of your child using the device. Until you go in and fix it, meaning delete them all individually, this device is annoyingly slow and unresponsive. I found out, you can get the apps to download or move them to the memory card, but it will still slow you down once that fills up and you still have to do regular maintaince on the devices memory. The first year of this is free, with this device, but I promise you it's more annoying than worth it. I was an early unlimited subscriber at $2.99 a month and I cancelled it rather quickly, even on my far better HDX and the first gen kindle it was STILL Annoying.

If you have an OLDER Child...this may be mitigated with a sit down conversation as to how their device works, what downloading means, and their storage space. My child is 5, and has proven to not exactly get the concept and download everything willy nilly if given the option.

Do yourself a favor....buy the HD Version, Pray they didn't cripple offline freetime on it, buy the extra warranty and case and and try that instead. That's what I plan to do, I'm going to give it a wait and see if they improve the HD device on the next round. Since the first gen HD 7 still works better than this one, I'll hold out.

Please Amazon....try to get it right next time.
Thanks,
Just another mom.

text_fidelity_a:
Archos 9 PC Windows 7 Starter Tablet (Black) Taken for what this is supposed to be, this is a fabulous machine. It's not a primary computer. It's not a laptop replacement. If you need a low power/ultra-portable computer, go with a netbook.

This is more of a mutt. It's a portable media player that doesn't have as much storage as an iPod or a Zen, but has a larger, higher quality screen and a kickstand, which makes it easier to watch movies at a desk.

It can read ebooks. It's not quite as light or comfortable for long term reading as a Kindle, but it can support full color images. It's far superior for this purpose than any of the other devices Amazon has put out an app for.

It can run Windows 7. It's not a full powered machine, but it's even smaller than a netbook.

It fits a slot somewhere between a PDA/smartphone and a netbook, and it's brilliant.

I would have liked a larger hard drive, an SD card (it would have gotten 5 stars if it had one) and more than one USB slot. There is no ethernet port. It only connects wirelessly. The optional port replicator gives you Ethernet and two more USB slots, but still no SD.

A few things to keep in mind. When you're first setting it up, you can't access the virtual keyboard button, so you need to use the Ease of Access icon to get to that. Windows will say to press the space bar to activate the feature. Use the mouse click button (marked +).

The design is very sleek. It's comfortable to hold and work with. The screen has an adjustable brightness, which is easier on the eyes, and easier to use in bright sunlight. The low glare screen helps with this as well.

Overall, this is bleeding edge, early adopter technology.
text_fidelity_b: Archos 9 PC Windows 7 Starter Tablet (Black)

ZAGG Limitless, Full-Size Multi-Device Universal Bluetooth Backlit Keyboard - Black I've been getting to the point where I have multiple tablets and mobile devices around the house that occasionally benefit from having a physical keyboard. I like that this one lets me switch between three paired devices with the push of a button.

It feels sturdy and the keys have a pleasant texture. It's bigger than previous bluetooth keyboards I've tried, which I think is in keeping with it being designed to be used with multiple devices. It's also kind of heavy, so it seems more like an around the house keyboard than a portable.

I like it better as an occasional keyboard than one to use all the time. it's too flat to feel ergonomic. The alt and command keys on the bottom row are all double size, which feels like a designer wanted a big space bar but didn't want to leave any empty space anywhere. The result is that they are easy to bump, which can send you off into menus. The slot for standing up a device on the back of the keyboard feels a bit close, and not wide enough for my Surface tablet in landscape mode, and portrait mode makes it fall over, so the stand is likely only good for things up to small tablet size.

Zmodo 1080p HD NVR WiFi System 4 HD Outdoor and 4 HD Indoor 1.0 Megapixel Wide Angle Wireless Security Camera with 500GB Hard Drive, Intelligent Recording, Smart Motion Detection, Web Access We have been using our 8cam setup for over a month and we are very happy with this purchase. The cameras were purchased to help us get our pre teen back on track. He recently got himself in trouble and we set these cameras up all over the house and eventually outside to keep our child honest.

Not only did it turn our sons behavior right around, but we now have an awesome setup to monitor our house when we are not around.

Although the software was not exactly very explanatory, I will pass along some of our learnings.

The software occasionally fails to give updates on alarms but resetting the phone seems to fix this right away. You do not have to purchase their cloud software to view the cameras: just plug an HDMI cable into the NVR and a mouse and you are set to view all the motion detections and recordings. I like how the cameras are not 1080p but are 720p. This gives our 500gb hard drive a break and we can record over a month on the NVR before overwriting data.

The NVR software was easy you setup and runs completely off of the device. The cameras were easy to setup and were plug and play.

I will eventually setup my router to port forward so I can remote into the recordings at any time although I don't think that will be necessary for our needs. I love the free alerts and its great to get the notifications on the phone to alert you of motion detected!

All in all this product was fantastic for what we needed and you can not beat the bundle price for the 500gb hard drove and 8 cameras! Thanks!
text_fidelity_b: Zmodo 1080p HD NVR WiFi System 4 HD Outdoor and 4 HD Indoor 1.0 Megapixel Wide Angle Wireless Security Camera with 500GB Hard Drive, Intelligent Recording, Smart Motion Detection, Web Access

We look at it as two steps above projecting on the wall and one step above projecting on a huge sheet, which is usually what we do. The sheet has worked fine, especially outdoors, but this is definitely better and is more than serviceable for our needs.  There's no creases, it doesn't wrinkle like the sheet can (or require ironing like the sheet), its heavier so it holds its flatness, and while not really heavy, it does do better when a light breeze kicks up.  It has grommets and comes with adhesive.  We use carabiners attached to our gutters if we're showing it outside against our garage and powerful magnets to attach it to a ceiling beam if we're showing inside. Motorola SURFboard SB6121 Cable Modem (SB6121) I read through Comcast supported model list and ordered this from another website, so I didn't have to pay their modem rental fee. I ordered Comcast using the online application process (borrowing a wireless connection from a neighbor), and was forced to order their starter package. Supposedly there is a way to refuse this if you call, but I didn't do this. I had a coax cable with me so as soon as I made my order I connected the modem to the coax input in the apartment, and my wireless router to the modem. I did not use a splitter. With my computer I tried to connect to the web which brought me to the comcast activation screen. I had no issues activating based on the info I had from the box and my comcast account number. This part was easy. It's a good thing I had my own cable since the starter package took two weeks to arrive.

My impression of this modem is that there is nothing special to this modem.You can access the modem through its IP address, which gives you several tabs: Status, Signal, Addresses Configuration, Logs, Open Source. No password is needed. You can remotely reboot it, and check to see if there is a signal. Other than that one feature I wished it had is having the ability to export logs. When the modem reboots, the logs get reset.

I have used a DOCSIS 2.0 modem at another location and I think the level of service makes a bigger difference than the DOCSIS version of the modem in use. You might see a difference if you pay for the top end ISP package, but I didn't get that. My plan is Performance which is supposed to be 50 Mbps, but my actual speed is 29 up 6 down.

I have read of some cases of the modem randomly rebooting. I don't have this issue. But I did open my modem and attached an aluminum heat sink as a precaution. I have managed to fit 100x25x10mm heatsink by cutting off a section. From what I read random reboots might be ISP related, but I'm not sure.

*****

As a side note, Comcast is terrible. At one point my service suddenly stopped. One tech service person I talked to hung up on me after half an hour of troubleshooting when see seemingly ran out of ideas to try. The next time I called I demanded a technician, which was scheduled to show up in 10 days at the earliest. I had a service outage for almost a month. The issue was a loose cable in their box. Also at one point my Netflix streaming was heavily throttled until Netlix payed off Comcast.
text_fidelity_b: Motorola SURFboard SB6121 Cable Modem (SB6121)
